preconditions.description: The number of cities n is between 2 and 20000, and the number of citizens m is between 1 and 10000.
There are exactly n-1 roads connecting the cities.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: Each road connects two distinct cities within the valid range [1, n].

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= n and 1 <= y <= n and x != y for x, y in citizens)
preconditions.description: Each citizen lives in one city and works in a different city, both within the valid range [1, n].
The roads form a connected tree structure, ensuring a unique simple path between any two cities.

postconditions.description: The total number of puppies k equals the sum of puppies given to citizens and guardians.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= c <= m for c in citizen_puppies) and len(set(citizen_puppies)) == len(citizen_puppies)
postconditions.description: The list of citizens receiving puppies contains distinct indices within the valid range [1, m].

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= r <= n - 1 for r in guardian_puppies) and len(set(guardian_puppies)) == len(guardian_puppies)
postconditions.description: The list of roads receiving puppies contains distinct indices within the valid range [1, n-1].

postconditions.expression: all(is_happy(citizen, citizen_puppies, guardian_puppies, edges) for citizen in citizens)
postconditions.description: Every citizen is happy: either they received a puppy, or every guardian on their shortest path received a puppy.
The total number of puppies k is the minimum possible value required to satisfy the happiness condition for all citizens.
